memory_candidates.content: The private-index overlay/commit/compare-and-swap git-plumbing primitive (mktemp GIT_INDEX_FILE; read-tree a base tree; per-path update-index --cacheinfo for add/modify or --force-remove for a path the target side deletes; write-tree; commit-tree -p <parent>; three-argument git update-ref <ref> <new> <old> for a true compare-and-swap, with the all-zero object id as <old> when the ref does not yet exist) builds one commit onto any base without ever touching HEAD, the shared index, or the working tree. Verified: a dependent commit's base-tree read is just the dependency's own built commit (its tree already encapsulates its own closure by induction), so no explicit recursive overlay of a whole dependency chain is needed.

scripts/lib/common.sh's lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh requires every common_test_resolve_subject call in a test suite to be paired with its own common_test_declare_subject call -- a suite resolving two subjects (e.g. the script under test plus a guard/library file) needs two declare calls, not one shared call. The migration from the older common_test_resolve_candidate (implicit deployed-then-source-store-then-sibling fallback order) to common_test_resolve_subject (explicit mode, exactly one deployed candidate and one source-store candidate) drops any third sibling-relative fallback candidate, since the two-candidate function has no slot for it.

git push is unconditionally blocked by this environment's guard-git-push.sh hook, including against a throwaway local bare/fixture repository under /tmp with no network or forge involvement at all -- the hook pattern-matches the command text regardless of destination. A test fixture that needs a remote-tracking ref (refs/remotes/<remote>/...) in a resolved state must fabricate it directly via git update-ref rather than a real push-then-fetch sequence; this exercises the exact same read path a real push would produce since the script under test only ever reads that ref's resolved value.

sapience_notes.subject: git push in this development environment
sapience_notes.value: Unconditionally blocked by guard-git-push.sh even against a throwaway local bare/fixture repository with no network or forge involvement; the hook matches command text, not destination. Fixtures needing a resolved remote-tracking ref must use git update-ref directly instead of a real push.

sapience_notes.subject: generate-context-line-counts.sh
sapience_notes.value: Refuses to run outside a deployed .claude/scripts/ tree, but its own header comment documents a REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bypass for a deliberate source-store invocation, avoiding the need to redeploy first just to regenerate a line-count index.

sapience_notes.subject: lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh
sapience_notes.value: Requires one common_test_declare_subject call per common_test_resolve_subject call in a test suite -- a suite resolving two subjects (e.g. a script under test plus a guard file) must declare both, not just the primary one.

sapience_notes.subject: this repository's origin/master branch
sapience_notes.value: Advanced from 414 commits behind HEAD to 4 commits behind within a single multi-hour task's own lifetime (plan time to implementation time), confirming this is an actively, concurrently pushed shared repository where a carried git-distance figure goes stale within hours and must be re-measured rather than trusted across dispatches.

sapience_notes.subject: a stacked-commit builder's dependency-readiness decision
sapience_notes.value: Can be made per-slice, per-invocation, from each dependency's own declared state field (merged vs not), processed in document order with an in-memory commit map, correctly stacking a dependent slice on its just-built dependency's commit within a single pass -- with no topological sort, union-find, or persisted build order -- provided the caller declares dependencies before dependents in the document.

sapience_notes.subject: testing a 3-argument git update-ref compare-and-swap failure
sapience_notes.value: A synchronous, single-threaded test can deterministically reproduce a real compare-and-swap failure by injecting a narrow, test-only environment-variable hook that moves the target ref between the script's own read of the ref's current value and its swap attempt -- no real concurrency or threading is needed to exercise this path.
